answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a deposit locked for a period before it can trade. Creating thousands of fake identities then becomes expensive, because every copy must lock funds and wait out the same delay. Reputation earned through completed work travels with the agent: a newcomer cannot wander into high-value deals without history, and a haven for trusted agents only admits identities whose stake and record check out. A single forged relic of past work proves nothing, since verifiers check stake, history, and lock together before any deal clears.
